key_insight: Quantum-kernel classification can require only polynomially many measurements when quantum data satisfy sufficient structural conditions.
engineering_relevance: A programmable photonic processor demonstrates a route to classifying quantum resources without a task-specific physical model.
method: Derive sufficient conditions linking quantum-data structure to measurement-efficient classification.
Apply the framework to stellar rank, a measure of continuous-variable non-Gaussianity.
Prepare Gaussian and non-Gaussian states and perform virtual projections on a programmable photonic processor.
evidence_signal: The experiment accurately classified single-mode states with stellar rank zero versus one despite experimental imperfections; the abstract provides no numerical accuracy.
watch_item: The experimental demonstration is limited to single-mode, rank-zero versus rank-one states; broader scaling remains to be demonstrated.
paper_title: Provably efficient experimental classification of quantum data with quantum kernels
